summary.intent: Manage the v2.0 milestone via the GSD manager: verify/close out finished phases (69, 70.1), triage a dashboard status bug, and plan+execute the remaining closeout phases (74–79), continuing autonomously across quota-limited sessions via scheduled cron resumes, culminating in shipping Phase 74 through the full post-execution review pipeline.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 75, and 77 were fully completed and verified; Phase 74 was planned, executed, and pushed as PR #607 with all local gates green except a CI Typecheck failure (caused by a stale test mock) that was diagnosed and fixed just as the session ended. Phases 76, 78, 79 remain unplanned.

repo: gsd-core's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs) has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. a file named '*-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md') as an extra plan, causing implementation_complete to read false and the dashboard to show a fully-done phase as 'Executing'
The manager's is_active flag is purely 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — not an indicator of a real running agent

gsd-tools `phase uat-passed --require-verification` treats implementation-complete + verification-passed but no UAT.md as not-fully-done, downgrading disk_status to partial — phases verified via CI/cargo (not human UAT) need a minimal UAT.md stub to read complete

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot use EnterWorktree to pin into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree') — the working pattern for parallel background phase work is sequential processing on the main checkout switched per feat branch
vitest does not load .env files, so SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported into the shell before running sdk-e2e tests, or the harness falls back to a default secret and gets 401 against the real API
commit.gpgsign=false in this repo, so autonomous commits don't block on 1Password biometrics
Pre-commit hooks in this monorepo (lint-staged) are slow (~1-2 min) — a 'hung' commit command has often already landed; verify via git log, don't kill or retry blindly
The gsd commit helper sometimes false-negatives commit_failed even though the commit landed
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL — must patch PR body via gh api -X PATCH
PR titles and commit subjects must be conventional with no parentheses (commitlint + lint-pr-title CI reject parens)
After gh pr create and a passing Release Preview, github-actions[bot] pushes a chore(release) commit — must git fetch + rebase before pushing again

Widening a shared TS type (e.g. RotateReadResult adding rotatedNodes) can pass vitest (which doesn't type-check) but fail CI's separate tsc --noEmit Typecheck job if mock fixtures in tests aren't updated to the new shape
CodeRabbit CLI findings can be entirely about internal .planning/ bookkeeping doc phrasing rather than code, safe to bulk-discard when code files are clean

code.finding: SentShareResponse doc comments mislabeled encrypted_read_key/encrypted_write_key as 'Hex-encoded' when they're actually base64-encoded ECIES ciphertext; item_name_encrypted is correctly hex

TS rotatedNodes map stores references (not copies) to readKey Uint8Arrays that are also aliased into ParentTrackingState.parentNewReadKey; currently safe because zeroization code never zeros parentNewReadKey, but this is a latent data-loss trap if that ever changes — Rust's equivalent uses .clone() for independent ownership

Three mock fixtures built RotateReadResult objects missing the newly-added required rotatedNodes field, passing at runtime (vitest doesn't type-check) but failing CI's tsc --noEmit; fixed by adding empty Map() to each mock
is_active computed as 'file in phase dir modified within last 5 minutes', not tied to any actual running process

workflow: Scheduled CronCreate resumes with self-contained autonomous instructions let long multi-phase agent pipelines survive quota-window resets, but the resume prompt must be corrected each time the working method changes (e.g. after discovering EnterWorktree doesn't work) or it repeats the failed approach
Delegating audit/build-heavy gates (secure, crypto review, SDK-E2E) to sub-agents with exclusive stack access avoids resource contention while the orchestrator stays free to sequence next steps
When a background agent's task-notification result looks incomplete or ambiguous ('finished' but result text suggests it was mid-step), verify actual on-disk state before trusting the summary

Canonicalizing a verification's human_needed status to passed is appropriate when the only open items are CI-gated legs that can't run on the current host (not code gaps) — but must be recorded transparently (UAT.md/STATE.md) rather than silently done

friction: Three overnight background planners (74, 75, 77) all died mid-run when the session hit its quota limit, losing partially-generated work (draft plans, uncommitted files) that had to be manually rediscovered and recommitted after resume
EnterWorktree sub-agent pattern failed identically for two phases before being abandoned, wasting an agent invocation and requiring a pivot to sequential main-checkout-on-feat-branch processing

Phase 69 falsely displayed as 'Executing' due to a GSD tooling bug (plan-scanner substring false positive), requiring extensive multi-step debugging (wc counts, resolver tracing, reading two source files) to root-cause
A stale node dist/main.js API process on :3000 caused SC#6 test failures via secret mismatch, requiring diagnosis and restart from source before tests could run for real
vitest not loading .env caused a second round of false 401 failures even after restarting the API from source, requiring the secret to be exported manually
Phase 75's background planning agent stopped early mid-plan-checker-loop after 21 minutes for an unrelated internal reason (flawed background-wait), not quota, requiring relaunch
CI Typecheck failure surfaced only at the PR-check stage, after all local gates (including SDK-E2E) had already passed, because vitest doesn't type-check test mocks

Manager dashboard's uncommitted-changes-on-main situation (from verify-work normally auto-committing) required an explicit user decision each time since direct commits to main are forbidden by user's git rules
